topline.text: Another quiet 24-48 hours nationally - no new DfE, Ofsted, safeguarding, SEND or funding announcement cleared the corroboration bar, so today's edition stays short rather than padded.
Anti-Bullying Week 2026 runs 16-20 November under the theme 'Break the Silence', set by the Anti-Bullying Alliance with input from 200+ children and young people.
topline.action: Worth slotting into next week's assembly/PSHE calendar now if it isn't locked in already.

topline.text: Reminder: DfE's call for evidence on exclusion reform closes in 9 days, on 19 November.

diary.text: Anti-Bullying Week 2026 - 'Break the Silence' theme; Odd Socks Day opens the week on 16 Nov.
DfE's call for evidence on school exclusion reform (behaviour strategies, in-school units, managed moves) closes - 9 days away.
DfE due to publish autumn 2025/26 suspensions and permanent exclusions statistics for England.

items.lede: Anti-Bullying Week sets 'Break the Silence' theme.
items.body: The Anti-Bullying Alliance has confirmed Anti-Bullying Week 2026 runs 16-20 November, with this year's theme - shaped directly by over 200 children and young people - highlighting that many still don't tell anyone when they're bullied. Odd Socks Day on 16 November opens the week, and free assembly, lesson and discussion resources are already available.
items.action: Useful lead time to build into next week's assembly/PSHE planning if not already in the diary.

items.lede: Exclusion reform feedback window narrows further.
items.body: DfE's call for evidence on exclusion reform - covering behaviour strategies, in-school units and managed moves - now closes in 9 days, on 19 November. The accompanying autumn 2025/26 suspensions and permanent exclusions statistics are still due this month, with no exact publication date yet confirmed on GOV.UK.
items.action: Last call for the inclusion team to get any evidence in before the window closes.

box.label: Jargon-buster - Odd Socks Day
box.intro: Seen it in Anti-Bullying Week materials and wondering what it means?
box.text: Odd Socks Day (16 Nov) is the Anti-Bullying Alliance's campaign opener - pupils and staff wear mismatched socks to mark that everyone is unique, used as an icebreaker for assembly conversations about bullying and difference.
